# 1. Executive Snapshot

- **The cheap tier now exists.** Claude Haiku 5.5 (Oct 7) is reported at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens under 100K-token prompts and about 75% cheaper than Haiku 4.5 (vendor claim, secondary sources). Sonnet 5.5 is reported to cut cache reads to $0.10/M. This closes the "Haiku-class vs Luna" comparison that has been open on our list: both cheap tiers are out, so the test can run now.
- **Gemini 4 Argon is not usable yet.** Restricted preview only; no GA date; the $2/$10 price is reportedly introductory and rises to $4/$20 (secondary). Do not plan around it.
- **Opportunity:** Google Cloud spend-cap budgets (preview, single project and single service) and Cloudflare Basin (open Iceberg-on-R2 data platform) are the two practical infrastructure items this cycle.
- **Risk:** Model names, dates and prices are inconsistent across sources, and the release cadence is fast ("model fatigue" coverage). Any decision made from a blog price is a decision at risk. Agent governance has still not been published (fourteenth report).
- **Recommended attention level: Medium.** Run the measurement work; ignore the launch noise.

# 2. Technologies Worth Watching

**Technology:** Claude Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 (cheap tier and cache pricing)

**Category:** AI / Cost

**What happened?**
Haiku 5.5 launched Oct 7 for high-volume work (summarization, classification, subagents) with effort controls. Reported pricing is $0.10 input / $0.50 output per M tokens up to 100K-token prompts and $0.50/$2.50 above. Anthropic says "around 75% less to run" than the prior Haiku, an average across workloads. Sonnet 5.5 reportedly lowers cache reads from $0.20 to $0.10/M, about 20% cheaper on typical agentic work. A Sonnet base price of $2/$10 appears in one source only.

**Why it matters?**
A 100K-token threshold means long-context jobs may cost 5x more per token than short ones. Cost per task depends on prompt length, effort and cache hits, not the headline price.

**Business Value:** Lower cost for routing, extraction, and subagent calls; completes the tiered design from earlier reports.

**Company Relevance:** 80

**Priority:** High

**Recommendation:** Pilot (verify prices on Anthropic's pricing page first, then add Haiku 5.5 to the eval set)

**Expected Impact:** Short

**Technology:** Gemini 4 Argon

**Category:** AI

**What happened?**
Google announced its flagship for multi-step work in coding, finance, law and security. Access is a restricted preview (reportedly via a partner program, cybersecurity first). Paid API and Ultra subscribers are "next" with no date. One reviewer got a 404 on the model ID on Oct 1. Output up to 1M tokens. Announced $2/$10 reportedly doubles after an introductory period. Launch date differs between sources.

**Why it matters?**
Announced is not available. Planning on it now buys nothing, and the doubled post-promo price changes the economics we would test.

**Business Value:** Possible third vendor for price leverage, once available.

**Company Relevance:** 45

**Priority:** Low

**Recommendation:** Observe (re-check when public API access and official pricing page appear)

**Technology:** Cloud spend-cap budgets (Google Cloud Billing)

**Category:** Cloud / Governance

**What happened?**
Cloud Billing release notes (July 27) describe spend-cap budgets in preview that pause new requests to eligible services when a project's spend reaches the budget. Limits: one project and one eligible service per budget; based on gross cost, ignoring credits; paused until lifted manually. A search result suggested an Oct 13 GA entry for a limited set of services; I could not confirm that.

**Why it matters?**
This is a hard stop, not an alert. It is the first vendor-native control we can map directly to the "spend caps" line in our own agent-control standard, if we use Google Cloud or Firebase AI Logic.

**Business Value:** Caps the worst case on runaway agent or API spend.

**Company Relevance:** 55 (higher if we run on Google Cloud)

**Priority:** Medium

**Recommendation:** Observe (use as a design reference for caps on our own cloud; confirm GA status in the release notes)

**Expected Impact:** Short

# 3. New Tools & Platforms

**Tool:** Cloudflare Basin

**Category:** Data

**What does it do?**
Announced Oct 1 as an open, serverless data platform built on Apache Iceberg and R2 to ingest, store, catalog and query analytical data. Pricing and maturity not verified (press release snippet only).

**Who should use it?**
Data and platform leads with analytics on R2 or S3 and a wish to avoid warehouse lock-in.

**Business Use Case:** Event, log and agent-trace data in an open table format that any engine can read.

**Estimated ROI:** Unknown until pricing is read; the open-format claim lowers exit cost.

**Recommended Experiment:** Load one week of agent-run logs into Basin and query it from a second engine, to test the openness claim.

**Estimated Evaluation Time:** 2-3 days (only after pricing and availability are confirmed)

**What does it do?**
Runs the same 30-50 real tasks across Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, GPT-6 Sol/Luna, and records cost per successful task.

**Who should use it?**

**Estimated ROI:** High; it is a precondition for tiered routing.

**Recommended Experiment:** Start with 20 tasks from our busiest workflow, three models, default effort only.

**Estimated Evaluation Time:** 3-5 days

# 4. Global Technology Direction

**Where is the market moving?**

- **Unit economics are the main competition now.** Cheap tiers (Haiku 5.5, Luna), cache-read price cuts, and effort controls all arrived within three weeks. The labs are competing on cost per task as much as capability.
- **Announcements are outrunning availability.** Gemini 4 Argon, GPT-6 variants and others show up as headlines with unclear access. Reported results are conflicting, so plan on shipped, documented APIs only.
- **Cost controls are moving into the platform.** Vendor spend caps and open data formats show buyers asking for hard limits and exit options.
- **Capital is part of the story.** Anthropic reportedly plans to disclose Q3 financials ahead of a possible IPO (secondary). That matters to us as a signal on vendor stability and pricing power, not as news to act on.

**Strategic implications:** Winning teams will have an eval set, per-task cost telemetry, and caps. They can then take each price cut in days and ignore each rumor.

## What This Means For Our Company

1. Our open cost-model refresh now has all the inputs: Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Luna. Do it once, with prices confirmed on vendor pages.
2. Build the tiered design on paper now: Haiku/Luna for routing and extraction, Sonnet/Opus for hard work.
3. Treat anything without a public API and a pricing page as a non-event.
4. Our agent-control standard should include a hard spend cap, not only alerts.
